evidence: Clear separation into logical modules: 'models', 'resources', 'auth', 'response', 'pagination', 'exception' under a single top-level package 'mendeley'
Low average fan-out (1.74) indicates modules depend on few others, typical of well-modularized monoliths
Directory depth of 4 suggests moderate nesting for organization without excessive decoupling (inconsistent with microservices)
No external service communication patterns observed; all functionality resides in one codebase with internal module dependencies
Shared domain models (e.g., Document, Profile, Group) used across resources and models layers
Resources layer directly depends on models layer (e.g., Documents resource instantiates UserDocument), indicating tight coupling within one process
Test suite organized in parallel module structure (test/manual, test/resources), mirroring production modules — common in monoliths
Single entry point (mendeley/__init__.py) exposing Mendeley class that orchestrates auth flows and session creation
risks: Tight coupling between models and resources may hinder independent evolution of domain vs. API concerns
Lack of explicit boundary enforcement (e.g., via interfaces or strict dependency inversion) could lead to circular dependencies over time
Monolithic deployment may scale less flexibly than microservices for high-throughput or heterogeneous workloads
